title: Reference mixbench and ensemble kernel selector for attention + prefill/decode regression suite
creator: Anika Rao
description:
Purpose: Build a compact, reproducible reference workload suite (mixbench) and an 'ensemble kernel selector' golden harness to validate kernel selection, attention tiling strategies, and prefill/decode scheduling across runtime releases. This ticket covers design, CI integration, and runbook for nightly canonicalization runs and PR-level perf checks.

Motivation: Recent regressions in kernel routing and decode latency (esp. long-context attention tiling) have been intermittent and hard to triage. We need a deterministic, small-enough golden suite that: 1) exercises kernel selection heuristics across model shapes, batch mixes, and seq lengths; 2) captures fragile attention code paths (tiling, flash-attention fallbacks); 3) validates prefill/decode scheduling interplay (prefill-heavy vs decode-heavy bursts).

Scope:
- Design mixbench workload corpus: a balanced set of traces (short chat, long-context summarization, multi-turn dialog, multi-query embedding + rerank) and synthetic microbenchmarks (attention tile boundaries, KV-cache stressers).
- Implement an 'ensemble kernel selector' harness that runs configured kernel candidates and records perf/latency/allocations & correctness checks for a single model and for a model family.
- Add attention-tiling-specific microbench (tiling thresholds, padding effects) with deterministic RNG seeds and input serializers.
- Build prefill/decode interleaving trace replayer to emulate realistic arrival patterns and to expose scheduling regressions.
- CI integration: lightweight PR-level checks (fast path) + nightly golden runs + regression detector that auto-files ENG tickets on statistically significant regressions.
- Documentation & runbook: how to interpret results, how to add new kernels, how to extend corpus.

Non-goals: Full-scale fleet benchmarking (handled by separate infra). Model retraining or architecture changes.
acceptance_criteria: Mixbench corpus created with >=12 representative traces and 6 microbench workloads
Ensemble kernel selector can run on a single GPU instance and output a canonical JSON artifact with kernels attempted, latency histogram (p50/p95/p99), token throughput, and memory alloc peak
CI fast-path validates new PRs within 10m and blocks merges on >5% p95 regression for target SLOs
Nightly canonicalization runs populate a Grafana dashboard and persist artifacts to s3://redwood-perf/goldens/eng-33847/
Runbook published with steps for reproducing a regression locally and for cribbing traces into the corpus
tasks: Design corpus and microbench definitions (owner: Marcus)
Build trace replayer for prefill/decode patterns (owner: Simran Patel)
CI integration: fast-path + nightly job (owner: CI team)
notes: Prefill/Decode interleave patterns: single big prefill followed by rapid decodes; steady-state decode stream; bursty multi-user multiplexing
Kernel candidates to include: fused-attention (optimized kernels), fallback generic kernel, quantized kernel variant, and small-seq specialized kernel
Metric targets: p95 latency drift < 3% vs golden baseline for non-regression; throughput drop < 5% for reserved bursts
Determinism: ensure RNG seeds and input normalizers are versioned alongside golden artifacts
Artifact format: flat JSON with metadata keys: model, commit_sha, kernel_candidates, trace_id, latency_histogram (buckets), mem_peak_mb, token_throughput
